# What xAI is told ganja is when a person logs in, and that a turn follows it.
#
# The record W4 of .omc/plans/2026-08-25-ganja-code-identity-headers.md gates
# on. This host has no seat roster to diff the way the codex backend does —
# x.ai's models come from the catalog rather than from a per-seat ladder — so
# there is no before-and-after here and none is implied. The gate was a real
# login and a real turn completing under ganja's own name, and this file is the
# record that they did.
#
# Unlike `codex-identity-probe.txt` there is no probe binary behind this one.
# It is composed by hand from the CLI's own stdout, relayed verbatim; the single
# edit is unescaping `&amp;` back to `&` in the authorize URL, which the
# terminal capture had HTML-escaped. Re-recorded by hand if the login is run
# again.
#
# Operator: W4 lane (Claude, lead-supervised); both legs run by the user
# Date:    2026-08-25
# Binary:  ganja-code 0.1.0, this tree's own debug build, run through cargo.
#          There is no vendor binary line here as P27's `*-posture-probe.txt`
#          fixtures carry one: those drove somebody else's CLI, and this drives
#          ganja against somebody else's endpoint. No machine line either — the
#          relay this was composed from did not carry one, and a plausible
#          guess in a recording is the one thing a recording is for not doing.

== leg 1: the browser login ==
# `ganja auth login --provider grok --method browser`
#
# What this leg is evidence of: the authorize query carries
# `referrer=ganja-code` — the moved constant, on the wire, in front of xAI —
# and the login it opened completed. The two credential stubs are the CLI's own
# masked rendering; no token bytes were printed by the run and none are recorded
# here. The `code_challenge`, `state` and `nonce` are one login's own
# single-use values, dead the moment it finished.

Go to: https://auth.x.ai/oauth2/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=b1a00492-073a-47ea-816f-4c329264a828&redirect_uri=http%3A%2F%2F127.0.0.1%3A56121%2Fcallback&scope=openid+profile+email+offline_access+grok-cli%3Aaccess+api%3Aaccess&code_challenge=gDFHxWy0SvpNq_T_oAY8bc4EQDskbaVffQ8GKyPjZg0&code_challenge_method=S256&state=hpEPagb13iklJYWpbihPC-AlHEyZ82buC-FiWwhUpDg&nonce=MJJdgq7IOjgFcnvsTK6YH8IGCIgJ2CwdtrjpH0qMUfg&plan=generic&referrer=ganja-code

login successful; stored the grok credential ****K99Q in /Users/zchee/.local/share/ganja/auth.json

== leg 2: one turn on the credential that login minted ==
# `GANJA_PROVIDER=grok ganja run "reply with exactly: pong"`
#
# The second half of the gate, and the half a login alone cannot give: a
# credential minted under the new referrer is one xAI's token endpoint accepted,
# and a turn served on it is that credential working against the API.

> build · grok-4.5
pong

== what this recording does not show ==
# The `User-Agent`, deliberately. Neither leg printed one — a login's stdout is
# the authorize URL and the CLI's own result lines, and `ganja run` prints the
# turn — so it is recorded here as unobserved rather than asserted. What carries
# it is `auth::grok::XAI_USER_AGENT`, which the divergence test in
# `auth::device`'s own tests holds equal to `GANJA_USER_AGENT` and unequal to
# `UPSTREAM_USER_AGENT`, for all three of this host's call sites at once. Both
# legs above ran on the tree where that constant already names ganja, so the
# requests carried it; that is a fact about the code, checked by a test, and
# copying the string into this file from the constant would make the recording
# a second copy of the source instead of a measurement of it.
#
# Also not shown, for the same reason: the token exchange's own request headers.
# They leave on a socket this process does not own, and nothing in either leg
# prints them.
